description:
FOUND s461ar (agent AR, round 18) while harvesting the drop census singles.
It owns the `perl-tests/sprintf2.t` census row, and it is a PPI structure bug
that has not been logged (docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md has no section for it).

perl reads a `{ ... }` at statement start as a BLOCK.  PPI reads it as a BLOCK
only when it has significant CONTENT; empty, or containing nothing but
comments, it becomes a PPI::Structure::Constructor inside an ordinary
PPI::Statement -- which then runs on and SWALLOWS the following statement.
PPI 1.291, `$doc->schildren`:

    { my $x=1; }  print 1;   ->  Statement::Compound<{ my $x=1; }>  +  Statement<print 1;>
    { }           print 1;   ->  Statement<{ }\nprint 1;>            (ONE statement)
    { # c only }  print 1;   ->  Statement<{ # c only }\nprint 1;>   (ONE statement)

Adding perl's own block disambiguator does NOT help: `{ ; }` is still a
Constructor (probed), so the `${;EXPR}` trick from task #463 item 5 does not
transfer.

WHERE IT BITES TODAY: perl-tests/sprintf2.t line 739, a block whose entire body
is comments (the `is(sprintf("%a", 0x0.b17217f7d1cf78p0 ...))` inside it was
commented out long ago with a PCL note about hex floats).  Losing the block
costs nothing; losing whatever the swallow takes with it is the actual price,
and it should be measured before this is scheduled.

FIX OPTIONS, none implemented:
  (a) A source-level repair: an empty/comment-only Constructor that STARTS a
      statement is a block, so give it a body PPI will believe.  `{ ; }` does
      not work; `{ 1; }` does (probed) -- but injecting a value into a user's
      block changes what a bare block at the end of a sub returns, so the
      repair would have to be limited to a block in void statement position,
      which is exactly where it fires anyway.
  (b) Treat it downstream: teach the statement walker that a Statement whose
      FIRST child is a Constructor with no significant children is a block,
      and SPLIT the swallowed remainder off.  That is the same "the lexer
      merged two statements" shape the #351 repairs handle, and it needs no
      source rewrite.
Log it in docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md (a new section) plus a docs/ppi-bug-report.t
row IN THE SAME COMMIT as whichever workaround lands -- CLAUDE.md rule 13.
subject: PPI lexes an EMPTY (or comment-only) bare block as an anon-hash Constructor -- and swallows the next statement
